Optional Ready-Made Gut Stacks
I don't think there's one supplement stack that heals everyone's gut. Whatever you take, the order matters. Get your digestion working mechanically first, then reset your diet and your gut motility, and only go after bugs and parasites with antimicrobials if you still have symptoms after that.

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: But some people want a ready-made starting point so they don't have to buy every ingredient separately. If that's you, I'd look for a "repair and rebuild" stack that has a probiotic you tolerate well (or a probiotic system), something prebiotic that helps your gut make short-chain fatty acids (butyrate especially), and nutrients for the gut lining like glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, mucosal-support herbs and so on.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text: Gemini suggested these kits to me, but so far they're the best ones I've seen, tho I haven't used them myself, so check the reviews. Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration covers all three of those (probiotic, prebiotic and mucosal support), so that's the general one.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text: Is it mainly leaky gut for you?

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit makes sense.

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: And Designs for Health GI Revive is one of the more complete gut-lining formulas, but on its own it's just the repair part of a gut protocol.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text: I wouldn't start everyone off on the general "gut cleanse" stacks either, the ones built around oregano oil, wormwood, black walnut, berberine or other antimicrobial herbs.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text: Those are for later (Phase 3), once you have more reason to suspect overgrowth, parasites, H. pylori or something else specific.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text: (My own advice is different for H. pylori, where berberine works well: see Parasites, above.)
